info.desc: Ray Charles’ initial foray into standards is a career highlight. For the first half, Charles’ old friend Quincy Jones crafts hard-swinging big band arrangements that match Ray’s band made up of musicians from the Ellington and Basie camps. Ralph Burns arranges the jazz-meets-string-orchestra second half, which features “Just for a Thrill” and “Come Rain or Come Shine.” The album showcased Charles’ breakout from rhythm and blues and onto a broader musical stage. Atlantic Records gave him full support in production and arrangements. As originally presented, the A side of the album featured the Ray Charles band with David “Fathead” Newman .

podcast.body: Another album arranged by Quincy Jones, contributing to his growing reputation as a hitmaker by showcasing his arranging skills for an established R&B chart-topper. "Jones began arranging his albums, including 1956's The Great Ray Charles and 1957's The Genius of Ray Charles."
